changes.after: Set a page's tab name and the information the browser needs.

before: `head` holds information about the document; `body` holds the page content.
`title` names the browser tab, while `h1` names the visible main heading.

Changing the title does not rewrite the heading. ```html Recipe archive

Today’s soup

```
`<meta charset="utf-8">` tells the browser how the file’s characters are encoded.

The viewport setting below lets a mobile browser use the device width as its layout viewport. It does not make a fixed-width design responsive by itself.
```html
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
```

`link` can point to a stylesheet without displaying link words on the page.
```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="recipe.css">
```
`rel="stylesheet"` says what the linked file is for. `href` says where to find it; the file must actually exist.
Place the charset, title, viewport metadata, and stylesheet link inside head. Keep the heading inside body.
after: `head` holds information about the page. `body` holds the content people use, such as headings and paragraphs.
`title` names the browser tab. `h1` is the main heading inside the page. They can have different words.

Changing one title does not change the other. ```html Recipe archive

Today’s soup

``` The tab says Recipe archive. The heading on the page says Today’s soup. These parts belong inside the page's `html` element.
`<meta charset="utf-8">` tells the browser how the file stores letters and symbols. Put it near the start of `head`.

The viewport is the area a browser uses to lay out a page. This setting lets a phone use its own width.
```html
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
```
It is a useful starting point for a phone layout. The page's CSS must also let its content fit.

A `link` element can load a separate CSS file. It does not show clickable link words.
```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="recipe.css">
```
Put this element inside `head`.

`rel="stylesheet"` says the linked file contains CSS. `href` gives the file's location.

The file must exist at that location. A link does not create it.
